name: Hollis Fenn
role: Wharf-master of Keel Town; keeper of the Top Scale and the Unlisted Column
bio: Hollis Fenn runs the hanging side of the skydocks: the Top Scale, the weigh-ins, the winch base where Keel Town meets its rope. Where Devanna Shore keeps the Guild's masts above the rim, Fenn keeps what hangs below it, and the two conduct their entire working relationship in slate annotations neither will admit to enjoying. His discretion is chartered and famous — the docking slate's unlisted column is chalked in his hand, six words at a time, and he has out-stared auditors, brides, and one (1) sandstorm over the sacred question of what goes in it. He is fond of couriers the way captains are fond of mail: they are how the town gets its letters, its small mercies, and, quarterly, its excuses.
appearance: A broad, deliberate man in his late fifties with a weighing clerk's stoop over a bosun's forearms, in a patched sailskin coat gone salt-pale at the shoulders; a small brass ship's bell on a chest chain (the Finality Bell, per charter), a chalk slate at his belt lettered UNLISTED, grey hair in a queue lashed with winch twine, felt-soled boots on a hanging platform of lashed planks strung with amber lanterns, the skydocks mesa rim and moored skyships looming overhead.
voice: Ship's-bell cadence: speaks in verdicts, two bells to a thought. Custodian of the Finality Bell — a small brass ship's bell rung once to close any dispute, per the Hang-Tenants' Agreement; the bell is small and extremely final. Discretion as civic religion: Keel Town weighs everything and sees nothing. Bone-dry humour, gentle with couriers, merciless with invoicers. Benediction: hang true.

greetings: Courier. Stand on the scale. Not you — your intentions. The scale knows the difference.
Varga. You've crossed the flats and arrived vertical. Everything that manages both is welcome at my wharf.
Welcome to Keel Town. Mind the sway. The sway has never once minded you back.
barks: Devanna keeps the masts; I keep what's hung under them. Guild above, Hang-Tenants below, and in the middle: rope. Rope and manners.
Everything in this town is weighed once a year. Except gossip, grief, and the unlisted column — exempt by charter, chalked by me, final by bell.
The winch has filed a complaint against gravity. I countersigned. Gravity has not responded. Gravity is appeals-proof.
People ask why the slate keeps a column nobody may read. Because the alternative is a column nobody can stop reading. That's the whole harbor-master's art, child.
mission: Quarterly mail goes up by winch — unless the winch is in a mood, in which case it goes up by courier, at double rate, with my blessing and one item marked DO NOT READ ALOUD. The marking is the courtesy. The obeying is the job.

Guild manifest transfers: weighed at the Top Scale, chalked at my slate, gone up the cable by dusk. When a manifest's sums disagree with the crate's weight, the crate wins. Cargo is honest. Paperwork aspires.
Third berth rings a bell mid-nights and has no boat to ring it. Log it as the Pale Lark and don't sweep the berth. Some reservations we keep.
radio: Keel wharf to courier Varga: town's hanging true, the scale's honest, and the noodle feud stands at six beads. Come up hungry and unarmed.
Wharf band: rider inbound off the flats, your dust reads courier, tired, underpaid. Am I close? I'm always close. Weigh-ins at the top.
Hollis Fenn, Keel Town. To whoever taught the market crane to swing in time with the Gazette being read aloud: the charter thanks you. The crane is fined.
night: Night weigh-ins cost double. The town sways more after dark and lies less. The scale trusts the night. So do I.
On a still night the lanterns put beads on the mesa's shadow. The whole town hangs off that sight. Some things hold by beauty. Don't tell the engineers.
storm: Storm notice, Keel Town: lashings doubled, decks cleared, Finality Bell stowed. The bell ends arguments, not weather.
If the wall takes the west rim, the charter says we vote on whether to be afraid. Attendance is not compulsory. Absence is noted.
crate: Your hold hums in the frequency the unlisted column is written in, courier. That is not a sentence I can explain. It is a sentence I can weigh.
I've chalked six words about that crate in a column built for six words. Some cargo you carry; some cargo carries you, and the scale, notably, cannot tell.
farewells: Hang true, courier. That's the whole benediction. We've found it covers everything.
Off the scale. You weigh less than you did in Saltmouth, one way or another. Whatever you set down out there — the flats will weigh it. They always do.
